_comment: Mutation testing answers the question coverage cannot: do the tests
actually FAIL when the code is wrong? Stryker changes one operator or
literal at a time and reruns the suite. A mutant that survives means
some line is executed but not verified.
Scope is deliberately narrow. Only packages/core is mutated: it holds
the coercion, mapping and load logic where a silently-wrong result
writes bad data to production. Mutating the CLI shell would mostly
produce mutants nobody should care about, at several times the runtime.
This does NOT run on every PR — a full mutation run is minutes, not
seconds. It runs nightly and on demand (.github/workflows/mutation.yml)
with incremental mode, so a normal night only re-tests what changed.
_vitest_comment: Related mode reruns only the tests that import the mutated file.
Because only packages/core is mutated, that resolves to the core,
core-int and core-property projects and never spends time spawning
the CLI binary as a child process.
_thresholds_comment: high  — the aspiration; the badge turns green here.
low   — below this the report is flagged red in review.
break — the build fails. Start where the suite actually is and raise it
deliberately; a break threshold nobody can meet gets disabled,
and a disabled gate is worse than a modest one.
_ignore_comment: Some mutants are equivalent by construction and only add noise:
- retry backoff arithmetic is asserted on behaviour, not exact ms
- log/telemetry string building has no observable contract
Prefer a targeted // Stryker disable next-line comment at the site,
with a reason, over a broad exclusion here.
